---
title: "P2 — Water and nutrition self-check"
---

Answer before opening the explanations. Explain one mechanism aloud and revisit
the [tutorial](index.qmd) if you can recall a term but cannot connect its steps.

## 1. Which potential is higher: −0.2 or −0.8 MPa?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

−0.2 MPa. Net passive movement tends towards lower total potential if a pathway is available.
:::

## 2. Calculate Ψ for Ψs = −1.0 MPa and Ψp = +0.6 MPa.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

−0.4 MPa, using the stated two-term approximation. Positive pressure and negative total potential can coexist.
:::

## 3. Do aquaporins pump water?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

No. They affect permeability; water still moves passively according to the potential difference.
:::

## 4. Why can waterlogging impair nutrient uptake?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

Low oxygen can restrict root respiration and ATP supply, impairing energy-dependent transport and other functions.
:::

## 5. Does stomatal closure improve every aspect of performance?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

No. It can conserve water while restricting CO2 entry and evaporative cooling. Outcomes depend on conditions and timescale.
:::

## 6. Are ten leaves from one treated tray ten independent treatment replicates?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

No. Shared tray treatment can confound treatment with tray conditions; within-tray leaves are subsamples.
:::

## 7. Does yellowing uniquely identify nitrogen deficiency?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

No. Ageing, other deficiencies, damage and environmental stress can cause similar observations. Context and measurements matter.
:::
